payload.problem_addressed: Equivariant Neural Networks (ENNs) lose expressivity on symmetric inputs because the output representation becomes invariant to more transformations than the input actually has ('symmetry increase'), and prior work lacked a rigorous, general characterization or reduction strategy for this.
payload.method_summary: The authors prove that for a given feature space and input symmetry group, the increased output symmetry is bounded below by a 'symmetry infimum' determined by the feature space's algebraic structure, give a computable algorithm (via orbit-type analysis) to derive this infimum and practical feature-design guidelines, and show that under manifold-hypothesis-style regularity, most equivariant maps (or sufficiently expressive ENNs) achieve exactly this infimum.
payload.contributions_summary: The paper gives a rigorous mathematical characterization of 'symmetry increase' in equivariant neural networks: it proves the increased symmetry has a computable infimum fixed by the feature space, derives an orbit-type-based algorithm and design guidelines to reach that infimum, and shows under regularity assumptions that generic equivariant maps attain it. Experiments on synthetic k-fold-symmetric structures and the real-world QM9 dataset validate the theoretical predictions and show the guidelines reduce harmful representation collapse.
key_architecture_choices: Feature-space design guided by orbit-type/symmetry-infimum analysis rather than architecture changes
Works with existing equivariant network backbones (SO(3)/O(3)-equivariant features) without relaxing the equivariance constraint
metrics: embedding difference norm / expressivity on symmetric graphs (GWL-test)
molecule property prediction accuracy with pretrained equivariant features
payload.headline_results: Guidelines derived from the symmetry-infimum framework empirically reduce symmetry increase (representation collapse) on synthetic k-fold-symmetric inputs and improve/validate molecule property prediction with pretrained equivariant features on QM9, matching theoretical predictions.
claimed_advantages: First rigorous, general (not case-specific) characterization of why and how much symmetry increase occurs in equivariant maps
Provides a computable target (the symmetry infimum) and actionable feature-design guidelines rather than relaxing equivariance
Applicable to general symmetry groups/feature spaces, not just the specific k-fold cases studied before
limitations: Guarantees are stated under 'standard regularity assumptions' (e.g. manifold hypothesis on data) that may not hold in all practical settings
Validated only on synthetic symmetric structures and one real dataset (QM9); no evaluation on non-molecular / discrete graph domains
payload.applicability_to_our_problem: Our B-rep face graphs frequently contain congruent/symmetric substructures (e.g. repeated faces from patterned or symmetric parts), which is exactly the setting where pointer/copy heads face orbit/symmetry ambiguity when addressing faces. This paper's symmetry-infimum framework and feature-design guidelines are a genuinely new (not our closed rotation-invariant-encoder) mechanism for reasoning about and reducing harmful symmetry collapse in our graph-transformer encoder's features, which could directly inform how we design pointer/copy addressing to avoid ambiguous ties between congruent faces.
payload.reviewer_notes: Highly theoretical (group-representation-theory heavy); applying it to our setting would require translating the orbit-type analysis from continuous SO(3)/O(3) symmetry groups to our discrete/mixed graph-symmetry setting (permutation symmetry among congruent faces), which is nontrivial. Code released at the linked GitHub repo, which may help validate applicability faster than re-deriving the theory from scratch.

provenance.problem_addressed: ENNs suffer from degraded expressivity when processing symmetric inputs: the output representations are invariant to transformations that extend beyond the input's symmetries.
provenance.method_summary: we prove that the increased symmetry is bounded from below by a unique symmetry infimum, which is determined entirely by the algebraic structure of the feature space.
provenance.contributions_summary: we provide a detailed and in-depth characterization of symmetry increase together with a principled framework for its reduction
provenance.headline_results: The results validate our theoretical predictions.
provenance.claimed_advantages: a rigorous understanding of its underlying causes and general reduction strategies remains lacking. In this paper, we provide a detailed and in-depth characterization
provenance.limitations: Under standard regularity assumptions, we demonstrate that for most equivariant maps, our guidelines effectively reduce symmetry increase.

payload.problem_addressed: Transformer-based CAD floorplan parsing methods infer spatial relationships only from semantic self-attention, without explicitly modeling geometric symmetry of building layouts, causing mismatched correspondences on long-range and symmetric spatial configurations.
payload.method_summary: PolarSym adds a polar-coordinate geometry-aware attention module that decouples geometric relationships into direction and distance, models each with its own constraint (directional for structural consistency, distance/radial for long-range symmetric correspondence), and fuses the two streams with a dynamic gating mechanism inside an otherwise standard Transformer architecture.
payload.contributions_summary: The paper proposes PolarSym, a polar-coordinate geometry-aware attention framework for CAD floorplan parsing that explicitly decouples direction and distance modeling and fuses them via dynamic gating, addressing symmetric and long-range spatial correspondence failures in prior Transformer-based parsers. It reports improvements over a reproduced SymPoint V2 baseline with faster, more stable convergence and low added computational cost.
key_architecture_choices: Decoupled directional and radial (distance) geometric attention branches computed in polar coordinates
Dynamic gating mechanism to fuse directional and distance branches
Preserves the vanilla Transformer backbone (attention module addition, not a full architecture replacement)
datasets: public CAD plan parsing dataset (floorplan, BIM-style drawings)
payload.headline_results: PolarSym improves 1.73% PQ, 1.54% RQ, and 4.31% mIoU over a reproduced SymPoint V2 baseline under identical training settings, with faster convergence and more stable optimization.
claimed_advantages: Explicit geometric symmetry modeling (vs. implicit positional encoding) improves long-range and symmetric correspondence matching
Faster and more stable convergence than baseline
limitations: Evaluated on a single public CAD floorplan dataset; generalization to other CAD domains (e.g. mechanical B-rep) untested
Method targets 2D architectural floorplans, not 3D B-rep geometry
payload.applicability_to_our_problem: The core idea — explicitly decoupling direction and distance into separate geometry-aware attention branches (in polar coordinates) with a gate to fuse them, specifically to resolve ambiguous long-range correspondences among geometrically symmetric/repeated elements — is directly transferable to our pointer/copy heads' face-addressing problem: our B-rep face graphs can have congruent or symmetric faces that are hard to disambiguate with semantic attention alone, and an analogous geometry-aware (direction/distance) attention bias could reduce mis-addressing when the pointer head must pick among visually/topologically similar faces.
payload.reviewer_notes: Domain is 2D architectural floorplans (BIM), not 3D mechanical B-rep, so the polar-coordinate parameterization would need rework for 3D face geometry; the mechanism (decoupled geometric attention + gating for symmetric-element disambiguation) is the transferable piece, not the specific coordinate system. No code link found in the text provided.
dependencies_on_other_methods: Point Transformer / SymPoint V2 baseline architecture

provenance.problem_addressed: they primarily infer spatial relationships from semantic features without explicitly modeling the inherent geometric symmetry of building layouts
provenance.method_summary: The framework explicitly decouples architectural geometric relationships into two complementary factors—direction and distance—and models them separately.
provenance.contributions_summary: this paper proposes a polar-coordinate geometry-aware attention framework named PolarSym for CAD plan parsing
provenance.headline_results: PolarSym achieves a performance improvement of 1.73% PQ, 1.54% RQ, and 4.31% mIoU over the reproduced SymPoint V2 baseline under identical training configurations.
provenance.claimed_advantages: This design significantly improves geometric modeling capabilities with minimal computational overhead.

payload.impact_rationale: A rigorous new framing for symmetry-ambiguity in our pointer/copy heads, but it's abstract group theory that would need real adaptation before it changes verifier pass-rate or pointer accuracy.
payload.effort_rationale: L-cost: requires translating continuous SO(3)/O(3) orbit-type theory to our discrete face-permutation symmetry setting and reimplementing the design guidelines — a research-level project, not a drop-in module.

payload.impact_rationale: Directly targets disambiguating symmetric/congruent elements via geometric attention, the exact failure mode our pointer heads face on congruent B-rep faces, though the gain is scoped to that subset of pointer errors.
